chapters.title: The Grasshopper and the King
chapters.previously_on: This is the opening chapter, so there are no previous chapters to recap. The book opens in the ancient Hayholt, where unusual activity surrounds the reopening of the throne room after three years of silence.
chapters.recap: Fourteen-year-old Simon is found neglecting his chores while exploring the Hedge Garden. Rachel the Dragon sends him to clean Doctor Morgenes' chambers, where Morgenes tells him the ancient history of the Hayholt, including its origins as the Sithi stronghold of Asu'a and the arrival of the Rimmersmen. Simon is fascinated and is offered the possibility of becoming Morgenes' apprentice. Meanwhile, the aging Prester John reflects on his mortality, his kingdom, and his sons Elias and Josua. Simon later witnesses Elias and Josua arguing bitterly over the succession and the dangerous priest Pryrates.

new_characters.name: Simon
new_characters.role: Young castle scullion and central viewpoint character
new_characters.description: A fourteen-year-old boy raised by the Hayholt's chambermaids. He is imaginative, easily distracted, curious about history, and frequently gets into trouble because his attention wanders. In this chapter, his fascination with Doctor Morgenes leads to the possibility of becoming the doctor's apprentice.

new_characters.name: Rachel the Dragon
new_characters.description: The strict head chambermaid responsible for Simon's upbringing and discipline. She constantly scolds him for his irresponsibility but clearly cares about his future and ultimately agrees to let him work for Morgenes.

new_characters.name: Prester John
new_characters.role: Aging High King of Osten Ard
new_characters.description: The legendary king is shown in declining health, sitting again upon the Dragonbone Chair. He reflects on his accomplishments, his sins, his mortality, and the future succession of his kingdom.

new_characters.name: Towser
new_characters.role: Prester John's elderly jester and confidant
new_characters.description: An old friend of Prester John who comforts him during his meditation on death and kingship. He listens patiently as John discusses Bright-Nail and his sons.

new_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
new_characters.description: A diminutive, eccentric scholar whose chambers contain strange devices, books, maps, experiments, and magical-looking objects. He teaches Simon about the history of the Hayholt and offers to make him an apprentice.

new_characters.name: Inch
new_characters.description: A large, slow-speaking assistant who arrives while Simon is visiting Morgenes. His appearance and behavior leave Simon with an uncertain impression.

new_characters.name: Josua Lackhand
new_characters.description: Prester John's younger son. Simon overhears him arguing with his brother Elias. Josua denies wanting the Dragonbone Chair and warns Elias about Pryrates, whom he considers dangerous.

new_characters.name: Elias
new_characters.role: Elder prince and heir to Prester John
new_characters.description: Prester John's first-born son and expected successor. He has returned from Meremund and argues bitterly with Josua over the throne, their past, and their family grievances.

new_characters.name: Pryrates
new_characters.description: A priest whom Josua warns Elias against. Josua says Pryrates has unhealthy interests and that the monks at the Usirean seminary in Nabban regarded him with suspicion.

locations.name: The Hayholt
locations.notes: The enormous castle is Simon's lifelong home. The chapter establishes that it was originally the Sithi stronghold of Asu'a and has been repeatedly altered by later peoples.

locations.name: Hedge Garden
locations.notes: Simon hides here while playing with a beetle and later notices a bird's nest. It is one of his favorite places to escape his duties.

locations.name: Hayholt Throne Room
locations.notes: The throne room has been closed for three years but is reopened for Prester John. The Dragonbone Chair and Bright-Nail are introduced here.

locations.name: Doctor Morgenes' Chambers
locations.notes: A strange laboratory filled with books, maps, experiments, animals, devices, and unexplained objects. Simon visits Morgenes here and receives his first serious invitation to become an apprentice.

locations.name: Hayholt Moat
locations.notes: Simon catches frogs here for Morgenes and later retrieves his forgotten broom. The moat also becomes the setting for an unsettling moment when Simon hears a mysterious whisper.

locations.name: Hayholt Chapel
locations.notes: Simon passes through the chapel and later hides in the choir loft, where he overhears the argument between Josua and Elias.

lore_notes.explanation: The larger land in which the story takes place. Morgenes explains that humans arrived after the Sithi had already inhabited the region for a very long time.
An ancient people who inhabited Osten Ard before mankind. Morgenes describes them as closely connected to the land and says that their civilization once extended across the region.
The ancient Sithi name associated with the stronghold now known as the Hayholt. The castle predates human memory and contains older structures beneath its later construction.

Northern seafarers who arrived in Osten Ard seeking plunder. According to Morgenes, they brought ironworking knowledge, giving them weapons that could defeat bronze weapons and even the Sithi's witchwood.
A major human kingdom on a rocky peninsula. Morgenes describes Nabban as an important source of guidance for other human peoples and notes its organized legions during the Rimmersmen's expansion.
Prester John's legendary sword. John describes it as containing a surviving nail from the Execution Tree associated with Usires Aedon and a relic identified as part of Saint Eahlstan.
The central savior figure of the Aedonite faith. Prester John treats the relic associated with Usires as sacred and connects his own kingship to divine service.
A martyred saint associated with the slaying of a dragon. Prester John says a finger-bone relic of Eahlstan is incorporated into Bright-Nail.
The great throne of Prester John, described as being made from dragon bones. It symbolizes the authority of the High King and is central to the succession concerns introduced in this chapter.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: The great castle; its name means High Keep.
The ancient Sithi name associated with the Hayholt.
The ancient Fair Folk of Osten Ard.
The land in which the story takes place.
Northern seafaring people who brought ironworking knowledge to Osten Ard.
The eccentric doctor and scholar of the Hayholt.
Prester John's younger son.
A priest whom Josua considers dangerous.

quotes.quote: A sword, small friend, is the extension of a man's right hand… and the end point of his heart.
quotes.speaker: Prester John

quotes.quote: I will have it back, manchild.
quotes.speaker: Unidentified whisper

theme_tracker.chapter_example: The Hayholt physically preserves layers of earlier civilizations, while Simon becomes fascinated by the people who lived there before him.
Prester John possesses enormous historical authority but is physically weakened, while his sons already struggle over the future of the throne.
Rachel believes Simon must learn responsibility, while Prester John understands kingship as a sacred obligation to God and his people.
Morgenes transforms Simon's desire for stories into a lesson about the real history of the Hayholt, the Sithi, and the Rimmersmen.
The aging Prester John faces the end of his reign while Elias and Josua represent the uncertain generation that will follow him.
Simon repeatedly abandons chores to investigate beetles, birds, frogs, strange objects, and the history of the castle.

foreshadowing.clue: The throne room has been sealed for three years and suddenly becomes active again.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: the unusual reopening establishes an atmosphere of change and uncertainty around the royal household.

foreshadowing.clue: Prester John believes he may not survive the winter and asks Towser to ensure Bright-Nail reaches Elias.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: the succession of the kingdom is already becoming an immediate concern.

foreshadowing.clue: Josua repeatedly warns Elias about Pryrates and calls him dangerous.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: Pryrates is introduced as a source of serious distrust within the royal family.

foreshadowing.clue: Simon hears a whisper promising that the Sithi will have their castle back.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: the ancient history of the Hayholt may not be as distant or finished as Simon assumes.

foreshadowing.clue: Morgenes unexpectedly decides that Simon might make a suitable apprentice.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: Simon's apparent uselessness may conceal abilities or qualities that others have not recognized.

discussion_questions: Why does Simon's curiosity make him seem useless to the people around him, yet valuable to Morgenes?
What does the chapter suggest about the difference between possessing power and being capable of using it?
Why do you think Williams begins the story by placing Simon, Prester John, and the ancient Hayholt in the same chapter?
chapters.map_update: The main setting is the Hayholt in Erkynland. Simon moves among the Hedge Garden, the throne-room area, Morgenes' chambers in the Middle Bailey, the moat, and the chapel. No major journey outside the castle occurs in this chapter.
chapters.readalong_prompt: As you continue, watch the contrast between Simon's restless curiosity and the adults' insistence that he become useful. Ask yourself: what might curiosity be preparing him to notice that other people cannot?

chapters.title: A Two-Frog Story
chapters.previously_on: Simon, a dreamy scullion, was introduced, as were the ailing King John, his jester Towser, and the eccentric scholar Doctor Morgenes. Simon was offered a chance to become Morgenes' apprentice.
chapters.recap: Simon, on his way to Morgenes' chambers, accidentally knocks over a suit of horse armor. Later, at the doctor's workshop, Morgenes tells Simon the history of the Hayholt and the Sithi. Simon learns of the Rimmersmen's invasion and the fall of the Sithi. Morgenes agrees to take Simon on as an apprentice. The chapter ends with Rachel, Simon's guardian, reflecting on the night he was born and on her raising of him, and Simon discovering a bird's nest.

new_characters.name: Inch
new_characters.description: A slow-witted, hulking man who helps Doctor Morgenes with heavy lifting. He seems simple and has a cow-like gaze, but his presence is unsettling to Simon.

new_characters.name: Jeremias
new_characters.description: A fat, somewhat lazy boy who is the apprentice to Jakob the chandler. He is a friend of Simon's and often accompanies him in his misadventures.

new_characters.name: Susanna
new_characters.description: A chambermaid who died in childbirth. She was a fisherman's widow. She is only seen in a flashback.

returning_characters.name: Simon
returning_characters.description: He causes another mishap by knocking over armor but continues his journey to Morgenes' workshop. His curiosity is piqued by Morgenes' stories of the Sithi and the Hayholt's history. He is also the subject of Rachel's memories.

returning_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
returning_characters.description: He tells Simon the history of the Hayholt and the Sithi, revealing his deep knowledge of the world's past. He formally agrees to make Simon his apprentice.

returning_characters.name: Rachel the Dragon
returning_characters.description: A flashback reveals her role in Simon's birth and her decision to raise him. She has a tough but deeply caring nature.

returning_characters.name: Jakob the Chandler
returning_characters.description: Jeremias's master, seen briefly.

returning_characters.name: Elispeth
returning_characters.description: An older woman who assisted at Simon's birth.

locations.name: Hayholt
locations.notes: Many different areas of the castle are described, including the chaplain's walking-hall, the Hedge Garden, and the moat. Simon's journey continues through different parts of the Hayholt.

locations.name: Morgenes' Chambers
locations.notes: The setting for the history lesson and the formal agreement to take Simon on as an apprentice.

lore_notes.explanation: Morgenes explains they were the first inhabitants of Osten Ard and built the Hayholt (Asu'a). They were a long-lived, magical people who were eventually driven out by the invading Rimmersmen.
Fierce seafarers from the west who brought iron weapons and conquered much of Osten Ard, including the Hayholt. They were the catalyst for the Sithi's decline.
A special type of wood used by the Sithi that was strong but could be defeated by the Rimmersmen's iron weapons.
A group of learned individuals who preserve ancient knowledge. Morgenes is a member, and his ring is a symbol of this.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: Morgenes' slow-witted assistant.
The chandler's apprentice.
Simon's birth name, given by his mother.

quotes.quote: A piece of writing is a trap... and the best kind. A book, you see, is the only kind of trap that keeps its captive—which is knowledge—alive forever.
quotes.speaker: Doctor Morgenes

theme_tracker.chapter_example: Rachel's memories of Simon's birth and Morgenes' tales of the Sithi show how the past shapes the present.
The history of the Sithi and Rimmersmen is a history of conquest and loss of power.
Simon's dreams are beginning to become a source of unease.
Rachel's sense of duty led her to raise Simon. Simon is starting to take on a new duty as Morgenes' apprentice.

foreshadowing.clue: Morgenes' cryptic mention of the Sithi's 'old magic' and his warning about 'false messengers'.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This hints at the mystical and dangerous elements that will become more prominent in the story.

foreshadowing.clue: The dream Simon has at the end of the chapter, with a voice whispering 'false messenger'.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This suggests future deception and peril.

discussion_questions: 1. How does the history lesson given by Morgenes change Simon's perception of his home, the Hayholt?
2. What is the significance of Rachel's memory of Simon's birth in this chapter? How does it shape our understanding of her character?
3. The chapter ends with a strange whisper. What could this suggest about the world Simon is about to step into as Morgenes' apprentice?
chapters.map_update: The main characters are still within the Hayholt, with Simon moving between different parts of the castle.
chapters.readalong_prompt: As you read, consider how Simon's new apprenticeship will change his life. What does the Hayholt's history of forgotten magic and lost peoples suggest about the story to come?

chapters.title: Birds in the Chapel
chapters.previously_on: Simon became Morgenes' apprentice and learned the history of the Sithi and the Rimmersmen. He also began having strange dreams, including a whisper warning of a 'false messenger.'
chapters.recap: Rachel reflects on her decision to let Simon become Morgenes' apprentice, remembering his birth. Simon finds a bird's nest and brings it to Rachel, who reluctantly lets him keep it. Later, in the chapel, Simon overhears a tense argument between Prince Elias and his brother Josua. Elias accuses Josua of coveting the throne, while Josua warns against the influence of Elias' counselor, Pryrates. The chapter ends with Simon being spied on by a mysterious boy.

new_characters.name: Prince Elias
new_characters.description: The elder son of King John and heir to the Dragonbone Chair. He is powerful, commanding, and aggressive. In this chapter, he is angry with his brother Josua, whom he accuses of desiring the throne.

new_characters.name: Prince Josua
new_characters.description: The younger son of King John, known as 'Lackhand' for his missing right hand. He is calmer and more thoughtful than his brother. He warns Elias against the priest Pryrates and expresses no desire for the crown.

new_characters.name: Malachias
new_characters.description: A mysterious boy who is seen spying on Simon and the princes. His motives and identity are unknown, but he appears to be watching both Simon and the royalty.

returning_characters.name: Simon
returning_characters.description: He finds a bird's nest and brings it to Rachel, who finally lets him keep it. He later spies on the princes' conversation in the chapel, which leaves him feeling uneasy about the world.

returning_characters.name: Rachel the Dragon
returning_characters.description: She reflects on Simon's birth and her decision to raise him. She has been thinking about her own past and is feeling the weight of her years. She is also the one who gives Simon permission to work for Morgenes.

returning_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
returning_characters.description: He is mentioned by Simon and Rachel, as he is the reason Simon is leaving his kitchen duties.

locations.name: Hayholt
locations.notes: The chapter takes place in several parts of the castle: the servants' quarters, the courtyard, the chapel, and a storage room. Simon's movement through these locations highlights the layered and secretive nature of the Hayholt.

locations.name: Hayholt Chapel
locations.notes: The setting for the central confrontation between the two princes. It's a quiet, sacred space that becomes the stage for a private, bitter argument.

locations.name: Hedge Garden
locations.notes: Simon has his conversation with Rachel here after she catches him with the bird's nest. It is a more peaceful setting.

lore_notes.explanation: The Sithi name for the Hayholt, mentioned as a reminder of the castle's ancient origins.
A priest and counselor to Prince Elias. Josua warns that he is a dangerous man with 'unhealthy interests,' suggesting he is more than just a religious figure.
Elias' deceased wife. Josua was escorting her when they were attacked, leading to Josua losing his hand. Elias blames Josua for her death.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: The elder prince, heir to the throne.
The younger prince, known as Lackhand.
A mysterious boy seen spying.
Elias's deceased wife.

quotes.quote: The crown is yours by right. The griefs we bear against each other need not worry you... I will not, do you hear me, will not be ordered out of my sire's house by anyone. Not even you, Elias.
quotes.speaker: Prince Josua

quotes.quote: Because of you, I stand a widower, and my daughter half an orphan. Do not speak to me of grief!
quotes.speaker: Prince Elias

theme_tracker.chapter_example: The bitter argument between Elias and Josua reveals the deep rift in the royal family.
Elias's claim to the throne and his suspicion of Josua's ambition drive the conflict.
Rachel's memories of Simon's birth connect the past to the present.
Simon's growing unease and the sense of unseen dangers continue to build.

foreshadowing.clue: Josua's warning about Pryrates and his 'unhealthy interests'.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This establishes Pryrates as a major antagonist and suggests his influence will be a key threat.

foreshadowing.clue: The presence of the boy Malachias, who is seen spying.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This hints at a network of spies and secret plots within the castle.

foreshadowing.clue: Elias's rage and his inability to forgive Josua.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This sets up the central conflict between the two brothers, which will drive much of the plot.

discussion_questions: 1. What does the argument between Elias and Josua reveal about their characters and the state of the kingdom?
2. How does Rachel's memory of Simon's birth and her decision to raise him deepen her character?
3. The chapter ends with Simon being spied on. What does this suggest about the world Simon is entering as Morgenes' apprentice?
chapters.map_update: Characters are still in the Hayholt, with Simon moving between the Hedge Garden, the chapel, and the servants' quarters.
chapters.readalong_prompt: Keep an eye on the relationship between Elias and Josua. How will their conflict shape the story? Also, who is the mysterious boy watching Simon?

chapters.title: Cricket Cage
chapters.previously_on: Simon began his apprenticeship with Morgenes and overheard the bitter argument between Prince Elias and Prince Josua, revealing the deep rift in the royal family. He also encountered a mysterious spy named Malachias.
chapters.recap: Simon begins his apprenticeship with Morgenes. He finds a cricket cage for his birds, but Morgenes warns him about the 'masquerade' creature living in it. Morgenes teaches him about the history of Osten Ard, the Sithi, and the fall of Asu'a. He mentions the siege engines, the battle of Ach Samrath, and a strange, terrible magic used by the Eri-king's son. Later, Simon and his friends go mushroom-hunting with Morgenes and discover a dead body in the forest, killed by an arrow.

new_characters.name: Isaak
new_characters.description: A young page from the upper residence. He is haughty and somewhat condescending, especially toward Simon and Jeremias. He is knowledgeable about court gossip.

returning_characters.name: Simon
returning_characters.description: He begins his apprenticeship, learns about the history of Osten Ard, and struggles with his reading and writing. He also discovers a dead body in the forest.

returning_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
returning_characters.description: He begins teaching Simon, both through chores and history lessons. He also reveals more about the Sithi and the fall of Asu'a.

returning_characters.name: Jeremias
returning_characters.description: He accompanies Simon and Morgenes on the mushroom-hunting expedition. Simon tries to help him join the guards.

returning_characters.name: Rachel the Dragon
returning_characters.description: She is mentioned as Simon's guardian and the one he must answer to.

locations.name: Morgenes' Chambers
locations.notes: The main setting for the chapter, where Simon begins his apprenticeship and receives his history lesson.

locations.name: Kynswood
locations.map_hint: Near the Hayholt, beside the Kynslagh
locations.notes: A small forest near the Hayholt where Morgenes takes the boys to gather herbs and mushrooms. It is here that they discover a dead body.

lore_notes.explanation: The Sithi name for the Hayholt, which was their greatest stronghold. It fell after a long siege by the Rimmersmen.
The son of the Eri-king, mentioned for the first time. He is associated with a strange and terrible magic that was used during the fall of Asu'a.
The site of a major battle where the Sithi and Hernystiri were defeated by the Rimmersmen. It represents a turning point in the history of Osten Ard.
A group of learned individuals, including Morgenes, who preserve ancient knowledge. Morgenes' work on King John's life is part of this.
Mentioned in the foreword and hinted at in Morgenes' stories. It is a figure of dread and mystery, linked to the history of the Sithi.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: The Eri-king's son, associated with terrible magic.
A western kingdom that was allied with the Sithi.
A young page.

quotes.quote: Books are a form of magic... because they span time and distance more surely than any spell or charm.
quotes.speaker: Doctor Morgenes

quotes.quote: The wise man is not waiting for the realness of the world to prove itself to him. How can one be an authority before the experiencing of this realness?
quotes.speaker: Binabik (in a later chapter, but fitting the theme)

theme_tracker.chapter_example: Morgenes' history lesson is all about remembering the past, both the glorious and the terrible.
The history of the Rimmersmen's conquest and the Sithi's fall is a story of power and its loss.
Morgenes' mention of 'strange, horrible magics' used by the Eri-king's son introduces a new, darker element of the world's history.
The discovery of the dead body in the forest hints at the growing dangers outside the castle walls.

foreshadowing.clue: The mention of the plague in Meremund and the discovery of the dead body.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This suggests a world in turmoil and the threat of violence spreading.

foreshadowing.clue: Morgenes' mention of the Eri-king's son and his 'terrible magic.'
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This character and his actions seem likely to be significant to the larger plot.

foreshadowing.clue: The dead man being killed by an arrow suggests someone is hunting in the area.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This could be related to the political tensions or a more personal threat.

discussion_questions: 1. How does Morgenes' history lesson change Simon's understanding of his world?
2. What is the significance of the dead body found in the forest? What does it foreshadow about the coming dangers?
3. Morgenes says books are a form of magic. How does this idea connect to the other themes of the novel?

chapters.title: The Tower Window
chapters.previously_on: Simon began his apprenticeship with Morgenes, learning about the Sithi and the fall of Asu'a. He also witnessed the bitter argument between Prince Elias and Prince Josua, revealing the deep rift in the royal family. A mysterious boy named Malachias has been seen spying on Simon.
chapters.recap: Novander is ending, and King John has fallen ill again. Simon goes to the Erchester market on an errand but is swindled by a con-artist monk named Brother Cadrach, who steals his purse. After returning empty-handed and facing disappointment, Simon climbs Green Angel Tower to escape his troubles. From the bell chamber, he sees a strange cloud of smoke on the horizon, which is later revealed to be Falshire burning. In the tower, Simon is spied on by the mysterious youth Malachias, who escapes. Simon is later caught by the sexton and forbidden from the tower, leading to his punishment.

new_characters.name: Brother Cadrach
new_characters.description: A plump, friendly-seeming Hernystiri monk who Simon meets at the Erchester market. He appears kind but is actually a thief who steals Simon's purse. He is not a true Aedonite man of faith.

new_characters.name: Princess Miriamele
new_characters.description: The daughter of Prince Elias. She is only glimpsed from a distance in this chapter, standing on a tower walkway. She appears beautiful and distant, a figure of longing for Simon.

returning_characters.name: Simon
returning_characters.description: He goes to the market, gets robbed, and faces the consequences. His mood swings from hopeful to despairing. He climbs Green Angel Tower and is caught, leading to his punishment and a sense of being trapped.

returning_characters.name: Rachel the Dragon
returning_characters.description: She punishes Simon for his carelessness by giving him a look of disappointment and extra chores.

returning_characters.name: Jeremias
returning_characters.description: He is mentioned as Simon's friend and occasional companion.

returning_characters.name: Malachias
returning_characters.description: The mysterious boy is seen spying on Simon again in the tower. He escapes when confronted, leaving Simon confused and frustrated.

returning_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
returning_characters.description: He is mentioned as Simon's new master, but he is not in this chapter.

locations.name: Erchester
locations.notes: The city where the market is held. Simon gets lost in the crowd and is robbed. It's a vibrant but dangerous place.

locations.name: Green Angel Tower
locations.map_hint: The tallest tower of the Hayholt
locations.notes: The ancient Sithi tower in the Hayholt. Simon climbs it to get a view of the world, but is caught by the sexton. This is a place of wonder and mystery for him.

lore_notes.explanation: A strange red comet appears in the sky at the end of the chapter, seen as an omen. It is a portent of significant change and bloodshed.
An earldom east of Erchester. In this chapter, it is revealed to be burning, indicating conflict and unrest in the kingdom.
A mysterious and dangerous people mentioned in passing. They are associated with the north and are a source of legend and fear.
The land is suffering from a drought, causing water shortages and hardship among the people. This adds to the sense of a kingdom in decline.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: The con-artist monk.
The city below the Hayholt.
Elias's daughter.
An earldom east of Erchester.

quotes.quote: When you were old, did your memories crowd out your other thoughts? Or did you lose them—your childhood, your hated enemies, your friends?
quotes.speaker: Simon (internal thought)

quotes.quote: A bearded star! An omen! The old king is dead, dead, dead! Long live the new king! A new age is begun!
quotes.speaker: Earl Fengbald

theme_tracker.chapter_example: Simon wonders about the nature of memory and aging, connecting his own small life to the vast history of the world.
Simon's daydreams and his desire to escape his life are central to his character.
The burning of Falshire and the appearance of the red comet suggest growing conflict and peril.
The comet is seen as an omen for a new age, suggesting a shift in power.

foreshadowing.clue: The Great Red Comet appears in the sky as an omen.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This is a classic portent of war, death, and significant change, setting the tone for the coming conflict.

foreshadowing.clue: The burning of Falshire.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This indicates that the kingdom is already in a state of turmoil and violence, which will only escalate.

foreshadowing.clue: Malachias is seen spying on Simon again.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This mystery deepens, suggesting Simon is being watched for reasons he doesn't understand.

discussion_questions: 1. How does Simon's trip to the market and his subsequent punishment reflect his character and his place in the world?
2. What is the significance of the Great Red Comet in the context of the story so far?
3. Why does Simon feel drawn to climb Green Angel Tower, and what does his punishment for doing so suggest about his future?

chapters.title: Six Silver Sparrows
chapters.previously_on: King John died, and Elias was crowned. Tensions between Elias and Josua grew. Simon was caught in the tower and forbidden from his favorite haunts. A red comet appeared in the sky as an omen.
chapters.recap: The chapter details the political maneuvering and growing tension in the Hayholt. Duke Isgrimnur confronts Elias about his northern lands, but Elias dismisses his concerns. Simon, still in trouble, is tasked with chores but finds comfort in the kitchen and daydreams about Hepzibah. Morgenes receives a secret message from Jarnauga warning of danger from the Norns. Pryrates confronts Morgenes, hinting at his own dark knowledge. The chapter ends with Simon lying awake, troubled by a strange dream and overhearing a conversation between Isgrimnur and Towser about Josua's disappearance.

new_characters.name: Sir Fluiren
new_characters.description: An aging knight, once a great hero, who serves as a counselor at the Hayholt. He is a reminder of the old days of King John and is distressed by the current conflicts.

new_characters.name: Hengfisk
new_characters.description: A stern, suspicious Rimmersgard monk at Saint Hoderund's. He is distrustful of strangers, especially trolls. He is a survivor of the attack on the abbey.

new_characters.name: Brother Langrian
new_characters.description: A young monk at Saint Hoderund's who is wounded and near death. He tells the story of the ambush that destroyed his abbey.

returning_characters.name: Simon
returning_characters.description: He is still in trouble but finds small moments of comfort. He has a fleeting romantic interest in Hepzibah and continues to feel trapped and unhappy.

returning_characters.name: Prince Elias
returning_characters.description: He dismisses Duke Isgrimnur's concerns about the northern lands, showing his disregard for his subjects' needs. He is becoming more isolated and arrogant.

returning_characters.name: Prince Josua
returning_characters.description: He is absent from this chapter, having disappeared from the Hayholt. His whereabouts are a mystery, but it's implied he has fled.

returning_characters.name: Duke Isgrimnur
returning_characters.description: He confronts Elias about the neglect of the northern lands. He is frustrated and increasingly concerned about the kingdom's direction.

returning_characters.name: Doctor Morgenes
returning_characters.description: He receives a secret message from Jarnauga warning of danger from the Norns. He is cautious but aware of the growing threat. He is also confronted by Pryrates.

returning_characters.name: Pryrates
returning_characters.description: He confronts Morgenes, hinting at his own dark knowledge and involvement with the Norns. He is revealed to be a dangerous and scheming figure.

returning_characters.name: Hepzibah
returning_characters.description: A serving girl who catches Simon's eye. She is flirtatious and has a beau, Lofsunu.

returning_characters.name: Towser
returning_characters.description: He is seen briefly, reflecting on the king's death and the strange happenings in the Hayholt.

returning_characters.name: Brother Cadrach
returning_characters.description: He is not present but is mentioned as the fraudulent monk who robbed Simon.

locations.name: Hayholt
locations.notes: The primary setting, with scenes in the castle's common areas, kitchens, and Morgenes' chambers. The political tension is palpable in every corner.

locations.name: Tourney Field
locations.notes: The location of a confrontation between Elias and Josua. It is an open, grassy area where the brothers spar and argue.

locations.name: Saint Hoderund's
locations.notes: An abbey that has been attacked. It is a scene of devastation and death.

lore_notes.explanation: Morgenes is a member. They are a group of learned individuals who preserve ancient knowledge. The message from Jarnauga suggests they are monitoring the Norns.
A mysterious and dangerous people from the north. They are also known as the White Foxes. The message warns that they are becoming active and pose a threat.
The mountain of the Norns. Its fires have been lit, indicating the Norns are mobilizing.
Mentioned in the foreword and Morgenes' stories. They are servants of Ineluki, the Storm King.
Also known as 'diggers.' They are dangerous creatures that have been attacking travelers in the north.

pronunciation_glossary.meaning: A stern Rimmersgard monk.
A young monk at Saint Hoderund's.
A member of the League of the Scroll.
Duke of Elvritshalla.
A priest and counselor to Elias.

quotes.quote: The air is full of birds today... They are easily captured, you know... and they hold so many secrets that the inquiring mind would find valuable.
quotes.speaker: Pryrates

quotes.quote: The king has an animal inside him, and Pryrates is its keeper...
quotes.speaker: Simon's Dream

theme_tracker.chapter_example: Elias's casual dismissal of Isgrimnur shows his absolute and uncaring hold on power.
Sir Fluiren represents the fading memory of a more honorable age.
Morgenes' secret messages and Pryrates' confrontation suggest a hidden world of magic and knowledge.
The news of the Norns' awakening and the attack on Saint Hoderund's indicates a growing, external threat.

foreshadowing.clue: The message from Jarnauga about the Norns and their fires.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This confirms the Norns are a real and active threat, setting up a major conflict for the series.

foreshadowing.clue: Josua's disappearance.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This is a key plot point that will drive much of the political intrigue.

foreshadowing.clue: Pryrates' confrontation with Morgenes and his hint at dark knowledge.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This establishes Pryrates as a major antagonist and suggests his connection to the darker forces in the world.

foreshadowing.clue: The attack on Saint Hoderund's and the mention of the Bukken.
foreshadowing.note: Possible clue: This shows the growing chaos and danger in the wider world.

discussion_questions: 1. How does the political tension between Elias and Josua manifest in this chapter? How does it affect the other characters?
2. What is the significance of Morgenes receiving a secret message? What does this suggest about the larger plot?
3. The chapter ends with Simon's dream. How do dreams function in the novel as a source of foreshadowing and insight?
